issues.legal_issue: A person in physical control of a site who has acquired an interest in it under an unchallenged agreement of sale may be in lawful possession for purposes of a cinema licence renewal even without having become the owner or lessee.
material_facts: The licensee had operated a cinema on the site under a lease that was due to expire.
Before the lease expired, one co-owner agreed to sell the licensee his undivided share of the property.
The co-owner also executed a lease of the remaining share and withdrew the objection to renewal, but the authority to grant that lease was disputed.
The agreement of sale was not challenged by the co-owner, and no subsequent interest was created that clouded it.
The licensee remained in physical control of the site, but was found not to have become its owner or lessee.
issues.conclusion: The licensee’s possession was lawful for the limited purpose of considering renewal of the cinema licence, and the licensing authority was directed to consider renewal on that basis, subject to the final adjudication of the title dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 11 of the Andhra Pradesh Cinemas (Regulation) Rules, 1970 required a licensee seeking grant or renewal to provide evidence of lawful possession. Lawful possession is wider than possession that is formally legal: it may be lawful where it is not forbidden by law and is supported by an interest that makes the possession excusable. An agreement of sale that gives a person in physical control an interest to hold or continue in possession may provide that basis even if it does not make the person the owner or lessee; an unchallenged interest of this kind is not merely litigious. Section 111(d) of the Transfer of Property Act illustrates the merger of an inferior interest into a superior one, while a tenant holding over may acquire lawful possession through the lessor’s express or implied acquiescence. By contrast, a tenant whose lease has expired and who has no continuing interest or acquiescence has no such basis, as distinguished in M.C. Chockalingam v. M. Manichavasagam. The remedy for forcible dispossession under the Specific Relief Act does not alter this distinction.

rule.if: cinema_license_renewal and physical_control_of_site and acquired_interest_under_sale_agreement and agreement_interest_uncontested

predicates.cinema_license_renewal: The proceeding concerns an application to renew a cinema licence.
predicates.physical_control_of_site: The licensee was in physical control of the site for which the licence renewal was sought.
predicates.acquired_interest_under_sale_agreement: A person in physical control acquired an interest to hold or continue in possession through an agreement of sale.
predicates.agreement_interest_uncontested: The interest acquired under the agreement was not challenged and was not clouded by a subsequent interest.
predicates.lawful_possession_for_license_renewal: The licensee is treated as being in lawful possession for the purpose of considering renewal of the licence.

issues.definition: When a licence-renewal proceeding concerns a licensee in physical control who acquired an uncontested interest through an agreement of sale, the licensee is treated as having lawful possession for renewal.
